page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5e.32xlarge is an x86_64 instance type from the Local SSDs family designed for extreme I/O throughput and high-density data workloads. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6763P-C processors running at a base clock speed of 2.9 GHz across 128 virtual cores, managed under the KVM hypervisor. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not present in this build, directing all platform resources solely toward compute, memory, and high-speed data processing.

Resource capacity is configured for substantial scale, offering 1024.0 GB of system memory, which yields an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Local storage is a defining characteristic, featuring an integrated 61435 GB SSD array attached directly to the host. In tandem with the storage infrastructure, the instance provides a high-throughput network fabric rated at a 320 Gbps baseline bandwidth, ensuring minimal latency and high interface capacity during cluster replication or massive concurrent transfers.

From an operational tradeoff perspective, the massive allocation of local SSD storage delivers exceptionally high sequential and random data access speeds directly on the node, bypassing network-attached storage latency. However, local storage requires administrative strategies for host-level durability, data redundancy, and automated snapshot management. The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides deep headroom for in-memory processing alongside storage-heavy tasks, eliminating standard memory bottlenecks.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5e.32xlarge is tailored for enterprise database management systems, real-time distributed analytical engines, NoSQL datastores, search index clusters, and large data warehouses that demand continuous high local drive bandwidth and high networking throughput.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5e.32xlarge is an x86_64 storage-optimized compute instance designed for intensive disk operations and large-scale data handling. Powered by 128 dedicated Intel Xeon 6763P-C cores operating at 2.9 GHz without GPU hardware, the system balances compute density with 1024.0 GB of RAM at an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Its primary technical highlight is an onboard 61435 GB local SSD array backed by a 320 Gbps baseline networking interface, which together minimize data transfer bottlenecks across external storage fabrics. Running on a KVM hypervisor, the platform avoids network-attached storage overhead for low-latency operations, making it suitable for distributed databases, big data analytics, transactional logging engines, and large-scale in-memory indexing platforms.
